- Recommended starting models: redwood-instruct-7B (quantized), and a larger eval against redwood-rlhf-13B for edge-case coverage.
- Benchmarks I will share: latency/cost estimates for both models, and a curated prompt set to run initial quality checks.

Action items we agreed: 
1) Acme to share ~200 representative prompts (real anonymized examples + known edge cases). Prefer CSV with columns: id, prompt_text, expected_behavior, sensitive_flag.
2) Redwood to provide baseline eval results and a suggested prompt set augmentation for regression tests.
3) Review redaction guidance and confirm any fields that must be removed/hashed before upload.

Subject: Re: Prompt set collection & redaction guidance

John — thanks for the note. A couple quick clarifications from the evaluation team: 

- Redaction guidance (high-level): remove or hash direct identifiers (names, emails, phone numbers). Replace account numbers with token <ACCOUNT_ID>. For nested conversations, keep thread context but strip quoted signatures that contain PII. We put a one-page checklist in redaction_guidance.docx in the Drive folder.
- Edge cases we care about:
  * multi-turn threads where the intent changes mid-thread
  * extremely long contexts (>4k tokens) to test truncation behavior
  * prompts that include markup/HTML or escaped characters
  * intentional adversarial phrasing (prompt injections)

- For the quantized 7B: it's great for cost-sensitive throughput but expect occasional verbosity and low-probability hallucinations on rare entity-resolution tasks. We will provide a short benchmark matrix comparing redwood-instruct-7B (q4_1) vs redwood-rlhf-13B for the sample set.

We'll also generate a set of synthetic edge-case prompts to augment your sample if you'd like — can do that after we see the initial CSV.

—Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Staff ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

John —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few final asks to make the eval as actionable as possible: 

1) Please use the template columns exactly (id, prompt_text, expected_behavior, sensitive_flag). Mark sensitive_flag as TRUE/FALSE. Do not include raw SSNs/credit card numbers — replace with <REDACTED> or <ACCOUNT_ID>.
2) If you can, add one column called "priority_check" with values high/medium/low to indicate which prompts are business-critical. We'll prioritize those in the initial run.
3) We'll share two links after our run: a Google Sheet with model-by-model example outputs and a short benchmarking dashboard (latency/cost/accuracy proxies). Expect those within 48 hours of receiving the CSV.
4) For compliance: confirm whether Acme requires pseudonymization only or full removal of identifiers. If it's the former, indicate which fields can be pseudonymized.

If useful, we can schedule a quick 20-min session to walk through the redaction checklist and the template. Otherwise, send the CSV to this thread and we'll start the evaluation.

Best,
